title: Rescue ghost variant contrast and icon-loading edgecases
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: After the recent token migration and compact density roll-up, we observed several regressions affecting the ghost / transparent button variant when used as icon-only and when showing an inline loading spinner. Symptoms include: 1) insufficient color contrast in dark themes for disabled and loading states, 2) spinner anchoring that shifts layout and increases hitbox jitter, 3) icon vertical offset in RTL, and 4) ghost borders disappearing under high-contrast themes. This ticket captures the design audit, proposed specs, and handoff artifacts to engineering for bug fixes and a regression test matrix.

Scope & impact:
- All icon-only ghost buttons across Console and SDK playgrounds.
- Themes: light, dark, high-contrast, and reduced-motion preferences.
- Platforms: web (Chrome, Safari, Firefox), and internal desktop wrapper.
- Customer impact: medium — visible UI regressions that can affect perceived reliability and a11y compliance.

Reproduction steps (minimal):
1. Sign into staging console with dark theme.
2. Navigate to Routes > Model Deployments.
3. Trigger an action that shows an icon-only ghost button with inline spinner (e.g., cancel deployment while action in-flight).
4. Observe spinner overlay causing 1–2px shift in icon position and ghost border alpha dropping below 3:1 contrast in dark themes.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Token migration introduced a semantic token rename (ghost-border-alt -> ghost-border-legacy) used by CSS fallback; dark theme token not mapped for icon-only combo.
- Spinner absolute positioning uses top/left nudge values tuned for LTR; RTL flip wasn't applied to the transform origin.
- Disabled/loading state relied on an opacity layer over the icon which reduces accessible contrast on already low-contrast ghost surfaces.

Design proposal / acceptance criteria:
1) Token audit: Introduce explicit tokens for icon-only ghost surfaces: surface.ghost.icon.border, surface.ghost.icon.bg, surface.ghost.icon.disabled-contrast. Map these tokens across themes.
2) Spinner anchoring: Update spinner layout so it uses transform: translate(-50%, -50%) relative to a stable 50%/50% anchor inside the icon container. This must be symmetric for RTL without separate codepaths.
3) Hitbox stability: Reserve spinner slot using a 1:1 square overlay layer so showing/hiding spinner does not change button dimensions or baseline alignment.
4) Contrast thresholds: For disabled/loading icon-only ghost, ensure color pair meets at least 3:1 when used on surface backgrounds; prefer 4.5:1 when icon conveys critical information. Provide fallback token values for high-contrast mode.
5) Reduced-motion: If prefers-reduced-motion is set, spinner should switch to a static progress indicator (pulsed opacity) to keep visual presence without motion.
6) Docs & examples: Update the Button component spec with: icon-only examples in light/dark/contrast, spinner overlay example, RTL screenshot, and a short guidance paragraph about when to prefer ghost vs. outline for icon-only actions.

Deliverables:
- Updated token mapping spreadsheet (Drive link below).
- Figma frames: new icon-only ghost states and annotated token callouts.
- Component spec doc with CSS/React examples and test cases.
- Small PR to runtime storybook and Console components replacing spinner anchoring and token usage.

Design decisions & tradeoffs:
- We intentionally pick a slightly higher contrast for icon-only ghost disabled state (3.5:1) than previous design to avoid ambiguity; this slightly increases visual prominence but preserves legibility.
- Using a symmetric transform anchor for spinner keeps CSS simpler but requires a one-off containment layer in the DOM. Slight DOM cost acceptable versus multiple nudge variants.

Acceptance criteria (QA):
- Visual regression tests added to Percy/Chromatic with examples for all theme combinations and RTL.
- Automated accessibility checks pass (axe-core) on examples for contrast and focus states.
- Manual validation notes for reduced-motion observed in Safari/Chrome.
- No layout shift observed in Lighthouse CLS tests for pages exercising icon-only buttons.

Artifacts & links:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/Buttons-Icon-Ghost-2025 (frames: IconGhost-States)
- Token spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/EXAMPLE-token-audit
- Design spec (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/EXAMPLE/Icon+Ghost+Button+Spec+2025-02
- Initial PR (engineering): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5821
- Storybook story: https://storybook.redwood-inference.com/?path=/story/button-icon-ghost--with-spinner

Next steps (short):
- [Design] Finalize token names and supply Figma frames (by 2025-02-12).
- [Eng] Implement token mapping and spinner anchoring in component (PR opened 2025-02-14).
- [QA] Add Percy permutations and run a11y checks (target 2025-02-18).

Notes for engineering handoff:
- Prefer CSS variables for tokens and avoid double-opacities (do contrast via foreground color tokens not opacity over icon).
- The containment layer should be position: relative; width/height equal to icon size (24/28 px). Spinner should be absolutely centered with transform translate(-50%, -50%). Use logical properties for alignment to be RTL-friendly.
- Provide an escape prop for the spinner to render as static indicator when prefers-reduced-motion is active.
